english: Then the wife said: 'Husband, where were you?' Then he said: 'I was working on the hill. I have grown tired.' [She:] 'Come into the house. Eat the grain (wheat). I was cooking it.' [He:] 'Where is the daughter?' [She:] 'She is sitting inside.' [He:] 'Wife, give me wine.' [She:] 'Drink the wine, and speak now.'
uncertain: h₁és: PST.2SG 'you were' (could also parse as AOR/IMP of h₁es- 'throw' or IMP 'be'); 'were' fits the question
pékʷom: PST.1SG 'I was cooking' -- speaker is the wife; could be 'I cooked'
speaker turns are not marked after the first two; assigned by sense
bʰh₂dʰí-kʷe nu: 'and speak now'; sentence-final nu is odd (maybe 'then/now'); bʰeh₂- 'speak' vs homonym 'shine'
puHróm: 'a type of grain, possibly wheat/spelt'

english: Whoever cuts off the beard of the father-in-law, let him give five gifts. Whoever strikes the mouth of the brother-in-law (husband's brother), let him give three rams. Whoever splits the cheek/jaw of the brother-in-law, let him leave the household (village). Whoever breaks a brother's shoulder, let him bring wine. Whoever strikes the queen, let him not live.
uncertain: h₁yós ... nu: relative 'whoever', with nu introducing the penalty clause
stunédeti: 'push, strike' -- 'strikes'
dayh₂urés vs swēḱurósyo: two different words for brother-in-law (husband's brother vs. brother-in-law, likely wife's brother)
ḱóymom: either the adjective 'kin, belonging to the family' or ḱóymos 'village, home, household'; taken as 'the household/village' he must leave
moysóns: 'rams/sheep'
mē gʷíh₃wet: mē + past (injunctive) = 'let him not live'

english: The queen has twins (twins are to the queen). The two brothers grew up. The two dwelt in the home (village). Then a wolf seized a duck. The two saw it, and the two killed it. The queen brought a gift to the brothers. Then the young one vanished (perished). The one alone (Somhos) lived. He worked. His fame is imperishable.
uncertain: yémHoh₁: dual 'twins' (also INS.SG); h₁stés 3DU 'are', with DAT h₃rḗǵn̥yeh₂ey = possession
ḱóymoy: LOC 'in the home/village' (could be NOM.DU adj 'two kinsmen')
gʷʰn̥tā́m: PST.3DU 'were killing/killed' (could be IMP.3DU)
h₂yéwHō: 'the young one' -- presumably one of the twins
somHós: 'the same / alone'; read as 'the one who remained alone', possibly a name
néḱt: 'vanish, be lost' -- may mean died
misfit: bʰréh₂tr̥bʰos: plural dative used for the two brothers where a dual would be expected (minor)

english: Then the sister said: 'Brother, I am thirsty. Give me water.' Then he said: 'Sister, drink. It has grown cold.' [She:] 'Don't push (hit) me!' [He:] 'I am not pushing you. Look at the duck. It is swimming.' [She:] 'I have seen the duck.' [He:] 'Now let it swim. Sister, I am afraid.'
uncertain: tód stéwdt: 'it (neuter, the water) has become cold'
stunéds/stunédmi: 'push, strike' -- 'push' or 'hit'
speaker turns after the first two are not marked; assigned by sense
snéh₂eti: SBJV 'let it swim / it will swim'
dedwóyh₂e: PRF.1SG 'I am afraid'; who is afraid and why is not stated

english: Then the guest said: 'Dawn has grown bright. Now I am going.' Then the host said: 'Take a gift.' [Guest:] 'Your gift is great. I shall remember your house. May your horses be swift. May Mother Earth protect you.' Then he said: 'Brother, may you live (long)!'
uncertain: sékʷt: two homonyms 'follow' and 'say'; 'say' fits
h₁áyso: middle imperative 'take, receive'
déh₃rom toy méǵh₂ h₁ésti: toy GEN/DAT -- 'your gift is great' or 'the gift is great for you'; speaker assumed to be the guest
meménoh₂: SBJV.1SG 'I shall remember'
final speaker (só 'he') unclear: guest or host

english: Gʷreh₂us ('Heavy') was ploughing the field with four oxen. And he set the boundary. And M̥h₂dh₂ros ('Wet') is the son of Gʷreh₂us. M̥h₂dh₂ros built a fence (enclosure). Mikros ('Mixed') was born of M̥h₂dh₂ros. Mikros bought a house for ten rams. Barley grew. Mikros lifted a quern-stone. Then he lay down (died), and Mother Earth covered him.
uncertain: gʷréh₂us, m̥h₂dh₂rós, miḱrós: taken as personal names ('heavy', '*wet' from root meh₂d-, '*mixed' from root meyḱ-); the last two have no gloss in the lexicon
gʷéwbʰis: INS.PL 'with cattle/oxen'
stnéh₂t: PST 'was placing/set'
moysṓys: INS.PL of price 'for ten rams'
tl̥néh₂t: 'was lifting' the quern-stone (maybe 'set up' a mill)
légʰt: 'lay down', likely euphemism for death given the earth covering him

english: The sheep said to the horses: 'I see a man, and he drives horses; my heart is pained.'
uncertain: dʰǵʰémonm̥: not in lexicon; read as ACC 'man (earthling)'
agʰnutor: not in lexicon; read as middle 'is pained/grieved' (Schleicher's fable)
h₂áǵeti: finite 3SG 'drives' where a participle 'driving' is expected; -kʷe on h₁éḱwoms links the clauses awkwardly
h₁ékʷoybʰyos: analyzer cannot parse it (kʷ for ḱw, -bʰyos dative plural); read as 'to the horses'
wewked: final -d and no accent, unlike the project's wéwket
orthography resembles a Schleicher's-fable variant rather than the project's notation

english: Then the father-in-law said: 'Daughter-in-law, bring wool. Clothe yourself with it. It is winter.' Then she said: 'Father-in-law, where are the sheep?' [He:] 'They are on the hill. The ram is standing in the fold (at the fence).' [She:] 'Father-in-law, I am afraid. A wolf is nearby (in front).' [He:] 'Daughter-in-law, do not tremble. I shall guard them. I am going to them.'
uncertain: téh₂eh₁ woséyeso: INS.SG fem 'with it' (the wool) + middle imperative 'clothe yourself'
h₂énti: 'in front, opposite, near'
tréms: mē + PST.2SG = prohibitive 'do not tremble'
tā́s h₁éymi: ACC of goal 'I go to them'
speaker turns after 'Then she said' not marked; assigned by sense
misfit: gʰórdʰe: VOC.SG of gʰórdʰos 'fence, enclosure' where a locative ('in the fold/at the fence') is required

english: Ǵr̥h₂éntih₂ ('Old Woman') was milking the sheep. A daughter was born of her. The daughter lifted (worked) wool, and the daughter clothed herself with it. The daughter is the mother of Dwiplā ('Twofold'). Dwiplā cooked grain. Dwiplā is the daughter-in-law of a father-in-law (the household's father-in-law). She protected the house. Ym̥tós ('Held') is Dwiplā's daughter. Ym̥tós raised a ram. Ym̥tós lay down (died), and Mother Earth covered her.
uncertain: ǵr̥h₂éntih₂, dwipléh₂, ym̥tós: taken as personal names ('old woman', 'twofold', 'held/restrained')
tósyeh₂s: GEN/ABL fem 'of/from her'
tl̥néh₂t: 'was lifting' wool -- odd verb; perhaps 'carried'
swéḱurosyo snusós: 'daughter-in-law of the father-in-law' (no named father-in-law)
h₂élet: 'was nourishing/raising'
misfit: ym̥tós: masculine o-stem name for a daughter, referred to by feminine tā́m (gender mismatch)

english: The horses said: 'Listen, sheep! Our heart is pained, seeing this: man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep has no wool.'
uncertain: whole item: recognized as Schleicher's 1868 fable text (akwāsas 'horses', krudʰi 'hear', manus patis 'man the master', warnā 'wool', gʰarmam wastram 'warm garment'); translated from that knowledge, not from the tools
wiwidwant- swas: 'having seen, (for) us/ours' -- read as 'seeing (this), our'
entire text: Schleicher-style late-PIE orthography without laryngeals or accents; the analyzer recognizes none of its 22 tokens

english: Whoever has a dog, let him feed it. If a dog kills (strikes) a man, the dog's master shall bring wine to the kinsmen. If a dog kills a wolf, let him rejoice. If a man strikes a dog, let him give a ram to its master. Let the dog guard the ram, and let the wolf not seize it. Let the dog not go into the brother-in-law's house. Let the dog lie down.
uncertain: ḱwṓ h₁yósmōy h₁éseti: DAT relative + 'be' = 'whoever has a dog'
gʷʰényēti: no gloss in lexicon; root gʷʰen- 'strike, slay'
gʰóstipotis: 'lord, master' (here the dog's owner); also 'guest/host'
ḱóymoybʰos: DAT.PL 'to the kinsmen' (could be ABL)
só mudyéh₁t: 'may he rejoice' -- referent (dog or owner) unclear
ní l̥gʰyéh₁t: 'may it lie down' -- purpose of this clause in a law unclear

english: Now hear what the king has decreed (established). Whoever steals cattle, let him pay ten rams. If a thief drives off two horses, let him pay four horses. If he hides the cattle and a watcher sees him, then let the watcher seize him. Whoever kills (strikes) a thief in the house, let him not pay. Whoever buys a ram from a thief, let him pay double.
uncertain: ḱluté: 2PL imperative 'hear!' (could be AOR.2PL, or VOC 'famous one')
h₁yód dʰéh₁t: relative 'what he has put/established'
kʷéyetu: no gloss in lexicon; root kʷey- 'pay, avenge' -> 'pay (compensation)'
h₁éḱwoh₁: dual 'two horses' (or INS.SG 'with a horse')
spéḱs: 'watcher, spy' -- a witness/watchman
mē kʷéyet: mē + past = 'let him not pay'
bʰrés: ABL 'from a thief' (or GEN 'a thief's ram')

english: Let the owner of a hundred cows bring ten cows to the king. He who has sheep, let him give wool to the queen. He who has a swift horse, let him lead it to the queen's daughter. Whoever hides a gift (tribute), let him pay double. He who has no cattle, let him give a gift (instead). May the king be a giver of good things.
uncertain: ḱm̥tógus: 'possessing 100 cows', i.e. a rich man
h₁yósmōy h₁ésonti / h₁éseti: DAT relative + 'be' = 'whoever has'
kʷéyetu: no gloss; root 'pay' -> 'pay double'
h₁áytu: active 'let him give'; the middle would mean 'receive'. 'Let him receive a gift' (the poor get one) is also plausible -- possibly the intended sense
dʰugtréy: spelled without h₂ (dʰugh₂tréy)

english: Whoever gives a pledge (oath), let him keep (guard) it. Whoever breaks a pledge, may Father Sky (Dyēus) strike him. Let Mother Earth hear the word. Let the Sun watch the pledge. If two brothers speak (dispute), let the two give a pledge. Whoever hears a pledge, let him remember it. Let the pledge be a bond.
uncertain: bʰoydʰéh₂: 'pledge, oath; contract'
bʰéh₂etes: SBJV 2/3DU 'speak'; homonym 'shine' does not fit
dédh₃tām: IMP.3DU 'let the two give' (or PST.3DU)
sh₂imṓ: 'something that binds; cord, rope' -> 'bond'

english: 'What do you want?'
uncertain: wēlh₁si: PRS.2SG of welh₁- 'choose, want' (no gloss on the stem; root gloss used); long ē noted

english: Then the father said: 'Daughter, a man has come to the house. He is looking for you.' Then the daughter said: 'Who is he?' [Father:] 'He is a rich man (owner of a hundred cows). The bride-price is ten gifts.' [Daughter:] 'I do not know him. Is he good?' Then he said: 'He is young.' [Daughter:] 'Let me look at him.' [Father:] 'May the gods bring you a good husband.'
uncertain: h₁wédmn̥: 'bride price, dowry'
sékʷt: 'say' (homonym 'follow')
spéḱyōh₂: SBJV.1SG 'let me look / I shall look'
wédʰoyh₁ent: OPT.3PL of wédʰeti 'lead, bring' (or homonym 'marry'); 'bring you a good husband'
final two speakers assigned by sense

english: Ǵérh₂onts ('Old') was speaking words. And the gods heard these things. Wipros ('Trembling') was born of him. And Wipros spoke words to the gods. The gods rejoiced. And PuHyos ('Purifier') was born of Wipros. His mouth was sharp. And PuHyos gave a ram to the Sun. PuHyos was sitting on the hill. PuHyos went away (departed).
uncertain: ǵérh₂onts, wiprós, puHyós: taken as names ('old', 'trembling, agitated', 'purifying')
bʰéh₂t: 'was speaking' (homonym 'shine' rejected because of wékʷōs 'words')
téh₂: neut. pl. 'these things'
h₁ést: PST.3SG 'was' (homonym AOR 'threw')
h₁opéyet: 'gave, offered'
léytt: 'went away' (homonym 'touch'); may mean died

english: Then the father-in-law said: 'Son-in-law, hear my word. Do not strike your brother-in-law. Carry water and wine to the daughter-in-law. Bring a ram to the gods. Do not steal the wool.' Then he said: 'Father-in-law, I am listening. I shall remember these things.' Then the father-in-law said: 'Son-in-law, protect the house. Son-in-law, may you live (long)!'
uncertain: méne: GEN.SG 'my' (could be imperative 'stay' of men- 'remain')
klépes: no gloss on stem; root klep- 'steal'; mē + PST = prohibitive
sékʷt: 'say' (homonym 'follow')
téh₂: neut. pl. 'these things'

english: A wolf seized the sheep. Then Belos ('Strong') killed (struck) it. He rescued them. And Dʰegʷʰros ('Burning') is the son of Belos. Dʰegʷʰros seized a thief, and the thief became afraid. Dʰegʷʰros led him to the village (home). And Slih₃wos ('Bluish') was born of Dʰegʷʰros. Slih₃wos slew the serpent. Slih₃wos's name is famous.
uncertain: bélos, dʰegʷʰrós, slih₃wós: taken as names ('strong', 'burning', 'bluish'; slih₃wós has no lexicon gloss, root 'blueish')
gʷʰént: PST 'was striking/slew'
tóm ḱóymom wédʰet: ACC of goal 'led him home/to the village'; alternatively 'led that kinsman' or (wédʰeti-2) 'bound him'
ḱlutóm: 'famous, heard of'
misfit: h₁sté: 2PL ('you are') where 3SG h₁ésti 'is' is required ('D. is the son of Belos')

english: Whoever kills a man, the dead man's kinsmen shall take ten gifts. If the kinsmen do not take them, then the slayer shall die. Whoever kills (strikes) a kinsman, let him not sit at the fire (hearth). If a brother kills a brother, let the watcher lead the slayer out of the house. May he lie in the earth with the dead. May his name be heard (famous).
uncertain: sléh₂gʷontor: MID.SBJV.3PL 'shall take'
gʷʰényēti: no gloss on stem; root 'strike, slay'
gʷʰonós: 'striker' -> the slayer
mr̥wṓys ǵʰémi ḱéyih₁to: INS.PL 'with/among the dead' + OPT.3SG middle 'may he lie'; the subject (slayer? victim?) is unclear; if 'the dead' is meant as subject it is in the wrong case/number
tósyo h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁syéh₁t: 'may his name be famous' -- odd as a penalty; perhaps of the victim
misfit: tóns: masculine ACC.PL 'them', but the referent déh₃reh₂ 'gifts' is neuter plural (expected téh₂)

english: Whoever buys a horse, let him look at the horse's mouth. Let him bring the price. Whoever buys wine, let him give a gift. If two brothers buy a house, let the two pay ten rams. Whoever does not give the price shall not take it. May the trading be in the village (among kin). Let a watcher (witness) speak the word.
uncertain: wósn̥ wéǵʰetu: 'let him convey/bring the price'
kʷéyetām: no gloss on stem; root 'pay'; 3DU
h₁áyeti: active 'give' (middle 'take')
tóm: masculine 'it/him' -- referent unclear (the horse?); wósn̥ 'price' is neuter
ne lémbʰeti: ne + SBJV 'he shall not take' (statement, not mē-prohibitive)
wesós ḱóymoy h₁syéh₁t: 'may the selling be in the village/household' -- sense unclear
spéḱs: 'watcher' as witness

english: Let the fence be the boundary. Whoever moves the boundary, let him leave the village. Whoever cuts the fence, let him give a gift. Whoever goes into a brother's field, let him not eat the barley. Let the hill be the border. Let the fence stand between the two fields. Let the owner of a hundred cows point out the border. May the boundary stand.
uncertain: Hyowdʰéyēti: causative 'cause to move'
ḱóymom: 'village/household' (noun ḱóymos-2) or adjective 'kin'
mē h₁édt: mē + aorist = prohibitive 'let him not eat'
sth₂éh₁yoyh₁t: OPT.3SG 'may it stand (firm)'

english: BʰruHros ('Brown') drove the rams to the hill. And H₁lengʰus ('Nimble') is the son of BʰruHros. H₁lengʰus led the sheep and milked them. And SomHos ('Same/Alone') was born of H₁lengʰus. SomHos built a house. And he killed a wolf. Great fame followed him. And he died, and his name is famous. Solh₂wos ('Whole') is SomHos's daughter. Solh₂wos wore wool. And they are famous.
uncertain: bʰruHrós, h₁léngʰus, somHós, solh₂wós: taken as names; bʰruHrós and solh₂wós have no lexicon gloss (roots 'brown', 'whole')
h₁ln̥gʷʰéws: GEN of h₁léngʰus with gʷʰ (root h₁lengʷʰ-), 'of/from H.'
gʷʰényet: no gloss; root 'strike, slay'
sékʷeto: middle 'followed'
wésto: middle 'was wearing'

english: Then the queen said: 'King, two men have come to the house. They are seeking our daughter.' Then he said: 'Who are they?' [Queen:] 'The old one is a rich man (owner of a hundred cows). The young one has nimble horses.' [King:] 'Let our daughter look at the two, and let her speak.' Then the queen said: 'May Dawn, daughter of the Sky, bring her a husband.'
uncertain: ǵérh₂onts: 'the old one'; h₂yuHnéy DAT 'the young one has' (possession)
h₁léngʰewes: 'light, nimble' horses
tóh₁: dual ACC 'the two' (or INS 'with that')
wédʰoyh₁t: OPT 'lead/bring' (or 'marry'): 'bring a husband to her'
speaker of 'Let our daughter look...' assumed to be the king
misfit: h₂isḱónti: 3PL verb with a dual subject ('two men'); a 3DU form is expected
kʷís: singular interrogative with plural verb h₁sénti 'who are they?'

english: Then the daughter said: 'Who placed the sun in the sky?' Then he said: 'The gods placed it.' [Daughter:] 'What drinks water and is never filled?' [Father:] 'The earth drinks it and is not filled.' [Daughter:] 'What lies on the hill and does not move?' [Father:] 'The boundary lies on the hill and does not move.' [Daughter:] 'What is red?' [Father:] 'Fire is red.' [Daughter:] 'Father, you know (everything).'
uncertain: riddle format: 'kʷíd ... tód' = 'what is it that ...'
pléh₁t: AOR 'become full'
Hyowdʰéyetor: middle 'be moved, stir'
séh₂: fem NOM 'she' (the earth); also parses as IMP 'become sated'
turns are unmarked after 'he said'; read as alternation: daughter asks each riddle, father answers, following the opening exchange and the closing 'Father, you know'

english: Ǵérh₂onts ('Old') the king slew the serpent, and great fame followed him. His son is a giver of good things. And the Giver gave gifts to the gods and to the kin. H₁lewdʰeros ('Free') was born of the Giver. And H₁lewdʰeros drove four swift horses. H₁lewdʰeros took a wife (married a lady). And their daughter is the mother of Gʷreh₂us ('Heavy'). Gʷreh₂us became king. Gʷreh₂us gave a name to his daughter (named his daughter). Gʷreh₂us died, and his fame is imperishable.
uncertain: ǵérh₂onts h₃rḗǵs: 'the old king' or a king named 'Old'
déh₃tōr: 'giver' -- used as a name/title of the son
dh₃trés: GEN/ABL of 'giver'
wédʰet pótnih₂m̥: 'led (home) a lady' = married
dʰugtréy: DAT 'to the daughter', spelled without h₂

english: Pl̥th₂enos ('Broad') had two horses. And the two horses were swift. Pl̥th₂enos was raising the two. And Bʰerǵʰus ('High') is the son of Pl̥th₂enos. Bʰerǵʰus yoked the two to the wagon (chariot). And H₂eḱros ('Sharp') was born of Bʰerǵʰus. H₂eḱros was driving a horse, and he carried barley. Great fame has reached him. He lay down (died). The horses' name is famous.
uncertain: pl̥th₂enṓy h₁stā́m: DAT + 'were (dual)' = possession
h₁stā́m: PST.3DU 'were' (also parses as AOR of h₁es- 'throw')
tóh₁: dual ACC 'the two' (or INS 'with them')
yunégt: 'was joining/yoking'
h₂élbʰit wéǵʰet: 'transported barley'
h₁éḱwōm h₁nómn̥: GEN.PL 'the horses' name' -- odd; perhaps 'his name among horsemen'

english: A guest (stranger) came to the house. Then the host said: 'Who are you? Where are you going?' Then he said: 'I am going to my brother. And I have grown tired. Let me sit at your fire.' Then the host said: 'Sit inside. Drink water. Guest, do not be afraid. May Dawn give you good things.'
uncertain: gʰóstis: 'guest; stranger, enemy'; gʰóstipotis 'host, master'
méne bʰréh₂term̥: GEN 'my' + ACC of goal
sédoh₂: SBJV.1SG 'let me sit'
